title: SK Hynix dropping a Nasdaq ADR on July 10, anyone else looking at this as a MU swap?
author: Kira1Cloud
selftext:
So apparently SK Hynix is going for a $29.4B raise, bookbuilding kicks off July 6, pricing July 9, Nasdaq debut targeted July 10.

Been comparing the two on moomoo this morning and the gap is kinda nuts. Similar market cap to Micron, higher estimated earnings, lower multiple. They already own the HBM and DRAM leadership story so they don't have to convince anyone they're "AI relevant", unlike half the names ripping green this year just for slapping AI on a slide deck.

My thinking: once US investors can buy it on the same screen as MU, some of that Korea discount, FX friction and liquidity haircut probably compresses. Not saying overnight, but the side by side is gonna be ugly for MU bulls.

Risks I'm chewing on:

\- new share dilution from the offering itself

\- memory is cyclical af, we've all seen this movie

\- if AI capex actually rolls over, both names bleed red together

\- the discount might just... Not close. Korea listings have stayed cheap forever

Not loading up day one, lessons learned from past hype IPOs. Probably watching the first week of tape then deciding if I trim MU into it.

Anyone else planning to rotate, or you sticking with MU?

comments.author: LarkoVelvet
comments.body: Every time I've tried the "cheaper comp" rotation it worked on paper and bled in practice. Korea discount exists for governance and geopolitical reasons that don't vanish just because the ticker moves to Nasdaq. I'd need to see actual US institutional flow building before I call this a real MU swap. Watching with interest but keeping my hands in my pockets for now.

replies.author: Kira1Cloud
replies.body:
Yeah this is the key distinction—valuation gap alone doesn’t force convergence without sustained flow.

The Korea discount isn’t a mispricing you can arbitrage cleanly; it’s structural (governance, geopolitics, index/mandate constraints). Until you see consistent US institutional allocation rotate in, it’s hard to justify it as a clean MU-style swap into Micron Technology.

Feels more like a narrative trade than a capital-flow regime change right now.

comments.body: I’ll wait for the IPO dust to settle and the Korea discount to start narrowing before I trim MU for SK Hynix.
